transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, honestly, I'm just so overwhelmed right now, and my husband practically begged me to come in. I mean, I work as a mechanic, you know? I’ve been at the same shop for years, and I know cars inside and out. I know every sound an engine makes, every rattle, every hiss. But lately... lately it's not car noises. What brought me in is that I keep hearing this voice. It's a man's voice. And he's not in the shop with me, but I hear him coming right out of the garage vents. At first, I thought maybe it was the guys playing a prank, hooking up a walkie-talkie or something, because it sounds so real. Clear as day, like somebody standing right next to me, breathing on my neck. 

And it's not just the vents anymore. Sometimes I’ll have my head under the hood of a Chevy or a Ford, just trying to check the alternator or something simple, and the voice comes right out from under the hood. And he says awful things. He tells me... he tells me not to trust my husband. He says my husband is doing things behind my back, plotting things. And then he’ll tell me not to touch certain cars. He’ll say, "Don't touch that one, it's a trap, they want you to touch it." And I just stand there, holding my wrench, terrified to move. I can't get any work done because I'm so scared of what he's going to say next, and I can't even go home and relax because I'm looking at my husband wondering if the voice is right. It's just... it's everywhere, and I can't make it stop.
About how long have you been hearing this voice?

Well, it's... gosh, it's been a while now. I remember it started right around the time the weather started getting cold last year, so... maybe about ten months? Yeah, definitely around ten months. Because I remember I was working on this old Subaru, doing a heater core replacement, which is just a nightmare job anyway because you have to pull the whole dash out, and that's when I first heard it. I thought maybe the wind was just howling through the bay doors, you know how it does in the winter? But then it kept happening, straight through spring and summer, and now we're almost back to winter again. Ten whole months of this guy talking to me. 

And it's not just the talking, it's... it's the feeling that I'm being watched, or tracked, or something. Like, for those same ten months, ever since the voice started, I've had this awful, creeping feeling that someone is keeping tabs on me. The voice tells me they are. He tells me that my husband is part of it, that they're all watching my every move at the shop, keeping a log of which cars I work on. I even started checking the undercarriage of my own truck for trackers, like those little magnetic GPS things you see in movies? I spend half my lunch break just crawling around on the concrete looking for them, getting grease all over my uniform for nothing, because I never find anything. But the voice says they're there. Ten months of looking over my shoulder, ten months of second-guessing my own husband... it's just exhausting. I can't even remember what it was like to just go to work and turn a wrench without feeling like I'm part of some massive conspiracy.
During these past ten months, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of severe depression or sadness?

No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I've been depressed or sad. Not like that. I've just been... terrified, mostly. And exhausted, like I said. But not sad. I mean, I still have energy to do things, you know? I get up, I go to the shop, I crawl under the cars, I look for the trackers. I'm always moving, always doing something. If I were depressed, I wouldn't be able to do all that, right? I'd just be lying in bed all day. But I can't do that. I have to keep moving, I have to keep checking things. 

Like last week, I stayed up for almost three days straight just mapping out all the different routes my husband could take to work, trying to see if he was meeting up with anyone to hand over the logs they're keeping on me. I had maps spread out all over the living room floor, drawing lines and calculating distances. You don't do that if you're sad, right? You do that when you're trying to figure things out. And I was feeling pretty good about it, actually, like I was finally getting ahead of them. My mind was just racing, going a million miles a minute, putting all the pieces together. I didn't even feel tired until the fourth day. So no, definitely not sad. Just... busy. And scared. But mostly just trying to stay one step ahead of whatever is going on.

Well, yeah, actually. It hasn't just been this past week. Honestly, if I look back at the whole ten months since the voice started, most of this past year has been taken over by those high-energy stretches. It's like... it's like a switch flips in my brain, you know? And suddenly I'm just going, going, going. My husband tells me I talk too fast when I get like that, like the words are just spilling out of my mouth before I can even catch them, and I'll start taking on way too much at the shop. I'll tell the service manager I can handle three engine rebuilds at once, which is crazy, right? Nobody can do that. But in my head, I feel like I can. 

I feel so driven, like I have this motor inside me that's redlining and I just can't slow down. I'll be bouncing from bay to bay, talking a mile a minute, trying to do a brake job, an alignment, and a transmission flush all at the exact same time. And the whole time, my thoughts are just zooming, connecting dots about the trackers and the logs and my husband. It happens a lot. I'd say the majority of the time since winter, I've been stuck in that overdrive gear. It's just wave after wave of it, where I don't need sleep and I feel like I can figure out the whole conspiracy if I just keep moving fast enough. So, yeah, it's definitely been happening over and over again, almost the whole time the voice has been there.
During these ten months, was there ever a period of two weeks or more where your energy and sleep were normal, but you were still hearing the voice?

Yeah, actually... there was a stretch. I think it was right around April, maybe early May? Because the weather was finally breaking and we usually get a huge rush of AC checks, but it was surprisingly dead at the shop for a couple of weeks. And during that time... I don't know, my brain just kind of shifted gears. I wasn't doing the million-miles-a-minute thing anymore. I was actually sleeping. Like, going to bed at 10 PM, waking up at 6 AM, getting a solid eight hours, sometimes even hitting snooze and getting nine, which felt so weird after all those nights staying up for days on end. 

I wasn't making these massive plans or trying to take on impossible jobs. I was just... normal? Like, energy-wise, anyway. I was just doing basic tire rotations, oil changes, taking my time, eating my lunch in the breakroom instead of crawling under trucks. But the thing is... the voice didn't stop. Not at all. Even during those quieter few weeks, when my body was actually resting and I wasn't bouncing off the walls, I still heard that guy's voice in the garage every single day. 

And I still knew—I mean, I fully believed with my whole chest—that my husband and my boss were tracking me. I'd be doing a simple brake pad replacement, totally well-rested, not rushing at all, and the voice would be right there in my ear, echoing off the concrete, telling me that the boss was watching me from the office window. It kept saying he was writing down exactly how long I took on the rotors, logging my movements, and that he was going to hand the whole file over to my husband later that night. So, yeah, my energy definitely slowed down and went back to normal for a good two or three weeks there, but the tracking thing and the voice? They never took a day off. It’s like they don't need to sleep, even when I do, you know? They just keep going.
